root_causes.description: The frontend container was killed (Killing: Stopping container frontend) and a replacement pod (frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8) was rescheduled, created and started, indicating a pod crash. The transient container termination explains the serving-gap swing in frontend request_rate, while no application error logs or error-rate spike were observed.

evidence.observed_value: container frontend stopped (count=1); replacement pod frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8 Scheduled/Created/Started
evidence.expected_baseline: no container kill events; single stable frontend pod set
application error lines present if fault were in-process (http_abort/high_latency)

root_causes.description: Elevated request-rate variability could alternatively reflect a brief frontend unavailability period with retries/backpressure, but the flat error rate makes an internal application fault unlikely as the primary cause.
Resource-pressure stress was considered but ruled out: CPU usage (mean 0.072) and memory working set (mean ~253 MB) stayed within normal ranges, and the 5m restart counter was zero.

evidence.expected_baseline: stable sub-0.1 CPU cores under normal load
no monotonic growth toward memory limit

remediation_steps: Confirm the frontend container termination cause via kubectl describe pod / last-state (exit code, OOMKilled vs external kill) for frontend-76cbddfbcc-* to determine if the crash was a kill or a resource eviction.
Verify the frontend Deployment reached full readiness after frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8 started and that frontend request_rate recovered to a steady baseline.
Ensure frontend has adequate replicas and a PodDisruptionBudget plus liveness/readiness probes so a single pod kill does not create a serving gap.
Add alerting on kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason and container kill events for frontend in otel-demo to catch future pod crashes early.
